('Territories, home bases and control','Summary lines 51-53','Rulebook pp. 4, 11, 17-18 and 29; extracted lines 258-303, 573-668, 864-964, 1459-1497','Home bases are not territories; lakes and Factory are territories; home-base entry exceptions; units override structure control; structure abilities remain with their owner except uncontrolled Mill production; defender retains control pending combat.'),
('Resource economy and destinations','Summary line 55','Rulebook pp. 4, 11 and 13; extracted lines 258-303, 573-668, 694-742','Only wood, food, metal and oil are resources; resources remain on board; any controlled territories may pay costs elsewhere; spent tokens return to supply; no resource or friendly-unit stacking limit.'),
('Basic Move and transport','Summary lines 61-64','Rulebook pp. 5 and 11; extracted lines 304-350, 573-668','Two different units, one step each, or one coin before upgrades; sequential movement; all units transport resources; only mechs transport workers; carriage does not consume a worker movement; river/lake distinction and default prohibition.'),
('Tunnels and hostile entry','Summary lines 65-69','Rulebook pp. 11, 15 and 18; extracted lines 573-668, 784-821, 900-964','Printed tunnels are mutually adjacent for all units; Mine personal tunnel; structure-only entry takes control; independent worker restrictions; undefended workers retreat immediately leaving resources at one popularity each; plastic-unit entry stops and initiates later combat; encounters stop character.'),
('Speed','Summary line 70','Rulebook p. 15 and p. 25; extracted lines 784-821, 1292-1343','One additional step for each selected character/mech; tunnel step costs one; mid-movement loading/unloading; hostile entry and encounters override further movement.'),
('Bolster','Summary line 72','Rulebook pp. 6, 12 and 18; extracted lines 351-402, 669-693, 900-964','One coin for two power or one combat card before upgrades; combat deck replenishment and exhausted-deck behavior; Monument adds one popularity.'),
('Trade','Summary line 74','Rulebook pp. 12 and 18; extracted lines 669-693, 900-964','One coin for two resources of any combination or one popularity before upgrades; resources placed on controlled worker territory; no resource Trade when all workers at home; Armory adds one power.'),
('Produce','Summary lines 76-87','Rulebook p. 13, p. 18 and p. 31; extracted lines 694-742, 900-964, 1539-1634','Full exposed cost paid first; up to two controlled territories before upgrades; one token per worker, placed locally; correct five terrain products and lake/Factory nonproduction; village workers removed left-to-right; optional production; workers never return to mat; newly exposed costs affect later actions.'),
('Mill','Summary lines 87, 95','Rulebook p. 18; extracted lines 900-964','Mill is a bonus production territory and produces as a worker; actual workers also produce; no actual worker required; no production on enemy-controlled Mill territory.'),
('Bottom action rules and Upgrade','Summary lines 91-93','Rulebook p. 14; extracted lines 743-783','Mat-specific full costs and coins; coins optional; completed actions remain available for coin/recruit benefits; oil Upgrade moves cube from green to empty bracketed red box, never solid-bordered red.'),
('Deploy','Summary line 94','Rulebook p. 15; extracted lines 784-821','Pay metal; any covered mech goes to controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability immediately applies to all character/mechs, excluding workers.'),
('Build and building abilities','Summary line 95','Rulebook p. 18; extracted lines 900-964','Pay wood; any structure goes to controlled worker territory; one structure total per territory; no lakes/home bases, Factory allowed; permanence; matching top action benefits, Mine universal movement access and owner-only abilities.'),
('Enlist and one-time benefits','Summary line 96','Rulebook p. 20; extracted lines 1014-1064','Pay food; recruit may come from any bottom section and occupy any open one-time faction bonus permanently; two power/coins/popularity/cards; ongoing bonus tied to removed recruit location.'),
('Recruit trigger, quantities and priority','Summary line 98','Rulebook pp. 14 and 20, PDF p. 10 Player Mat image X5924; extracted lines 743-783, 1014-1064','Self and immediate neighbors trigger matching bottom action; top/Factory/encounter actions excluded; active then left then right; two-player opponent counted once; Upgrade power, Deploy coin, Build popularity, Enlist combat card, one each.'),
('All faction starting abilities','Summary lines 102-110','Rulebook p. 21; extracted lines 1065-1109','Relentless includes Factory; Coercion once per turn one card equals one resource independent of card value; Swim workers only, rivers but not lakes; Meander two different choices on one card in either order with gains usable for second cost; Dominate retains second objective and removes combat-star cap.'),
('All five Riverwalk destinations','Summary lines 104-110','Rulebook pp. 15-17; extracted lines 784-899','Saxony/Nordic forests and mountains; Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Polania villages and mountains; character/mechs only.'),
('Saxony mech abilities','Summary line 114','Rulebook p. 15; extracted lines 784-821','Underpass joins controlled mountains and tunnels including own Mine; Disarm causes opponent two track-power loss before tunnel/Mine combat once per combat.'),
('Rusviet mech abilities','Summary line 115','Rulebook p. 16; extracted lines 822-863','Township joins controlled villages with Factory; People\u2019s Army grants one extra combat card total if any friendly worker present, still requires plastic combat unit; example correct.'),
('Nordic mech abilities','Summary lines 116, 120, 166','Rulebook p. 16; extracted lines 822-863','Seaworthy permits lake movement and optional adjacent-lake retreats including carried workers; Artillery costs one track power to remove two opponent power, once per combat.'),
('Crimea mech abilities','Summary line 117','Rulebook p. 17; extracted lines 864-899','Wayfare from territory/home to own or any inactive home, including expansion placeholders regardless of distance; Scout steals random combat card once per combat.'),
('Polania mech abilities and lake restrictions','Summary lines 118-120','Rulebook pp. 16-17; extracted lines 822-899','Submerge lake-to-lake movement; Camaraderie applies after won attacking combat rather than undefended worker displacement; workers/resources cannot be abandoned on lakes; workers need mech to leave; no deploy/build on lake; lake combat; only Nordic gets lake-retreat exception.'),
('Star conditions and permanence','Summary line 126','Rulebook pp. 21 and 27; extracted lines 1065-1109, 1375-1400','All nine goal categories and exact quantities, compulsory placement except choice of objective reveal, two normal combat stars, Saxony exception, goal sharing and star permanence.'),
('Immediate end, bottom-action benefits and pending combat','Summary lines 128, 169','Rulebook pp. 20, 23 and 28; extracted lines 1014-1064, 1172-1244, 1401-1458','Sixth star stops further turns/actions/encounters; bottom action yields primary benefit/coins/own recruit benefit before star; neighbor recruit star order; pending movement into unresolved combat is undone.'),
('Scoring categories and popularity table','Summary lines 132-140','Rulebook pp. 28-29, especially PDF p. 29 track image X6598; extracted lines 1401-1497','Held coins plus stars, territories and pooled resource pairs; lakes count, homes excluded, Factory three total; 0-6 payouts 3/2/1, 7-12 payouts 4/3/2, 13-18 payouts 5/4/3; odd resource ignored; arithmetic example 20+21+12=53 verified.'),
('All six structure tiles and exact payouts','Summary lines 142-153','Rulebook p. 19 tile images X6427, X6429, X6431, X6433, X6435, X6437; extracted lines 965-1013; p. 29, extracted lines 1459-1497','Visually inspected all six source-PDF tile assets: adjacent tunnels 1/2-3/4-5/6 pays 2/4/6/9; adjacent lakes and encounters 1/2-3/4-5/6-7 pays 2/4/6/9; on tunnels 1/2/3-4 pays 2/4/6; row and combined farms/tundras 1/2/3/4 pays 2/4/6/9. Unique feature counting, removed encounters, Mine exclusion, longest straight line, rivers, zero and enemy control handled correctly.'),
('Winner and complete tie order','Summary line 155','Rulebook p. 29, Declaring the Winner; extracted lines 1480-1497','Most coins; workers+mechs+structures excluding character; power; popularity; controlled resources; controlled territories; placed stars.'),
('Combat timing and commitments','Summary lines 161-165','Rulebook p. 22 and p. 23; extracted lines 1110-1244','All movement first, then chosen combat order before bottom action; attack allowed at zero power/popularity; attacker ability first; dial 0-7 capped by available track power; one optional card per participating plastic unit plus People\u2019s Army; simultaneous reveal; attacker wins ties; both pay dial and discard used cards face-up; cards do not cost track power.'),

A Factory card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); its actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement/stop rules apply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Factory: ‘Every player’s character’ on first finish; at most one permanent card; fifth action section; no mat/recruit benefits; bottom Move distance and Speed."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective. You must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony retains the other card after the first and may score both.","support":"supported","evidence":"Objectives and agreements: ‘Only on your own turn’; meet all requirements at reveal; place star and both cards on deck bottom; Saxony retains other card and can score both."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"Stars are earned for six upgrades; four deployed mechs; four built structures; four recruits; all eight workers on the board; one revealed completed objective; a combat victory (up to two stars, except Saxony); 18 popularity; or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony’s exception. Stars are permanent once placed even if power or popularity later falls, and other players’ stars do not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends the game with no equalizing turns or further actions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars and immediate end: full achievement list; goals awarded once; ‘A placed star is permanent’; other stars never block; sixth star immediately ends play."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to their prior territories; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, and right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step. If an earlier player places the sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.","support":"supported","evidence":"Sixth-star sequence: ‘primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing’; pending battle movement undone; active, left, right sequence and stop rule."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus Factory count as seven territories and add $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs and add $12, total $53 in addition to held coins. The selected structure bonus is also scored, even if enemies control your structure territories. Tiebreakers, in order: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Final fortune table and example: ‘$20 + $21 + $12 = $53’; structure bonus even if enemies control; tie-break order."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea’s unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: ‘A home base is not a territory’; default restrictions and exceptions; inactive expansion placeholders."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"Mountain produces metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, and village a worker. Lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce terrain table; resources definition says workers are not resources; ‘Resource tokens have no supply limit: use multipliers if needed.’"},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; a mech may also carry any number of your workers, but never your character. A carried worker may move itself later in the turn. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, with the extra Speed step usable before or after it. A mech can pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Enemy-unit stops and character encounter stops override Speed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: unit carrying rules; Speed: adds one territory, tunnel jump costs one step, extra step before/after; stops override Speed."},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit type.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: ‘All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit’; ‘Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure.’"},
    {"id":"Q25","answer":"You do not have to pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, move your token to a different section and take neither action; this is a legal dead turn. You must move the token, and never pay only part of a cost.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: ‘If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn’; ‘Never pay only part of a cost.’"},
    {"id":"Q26","answer":"A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are matching top-action bonuses. You keep a building’s abilities even without controlling its territory, and enemy units do not gain them, so an enemy occupant does not take them away.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bolster/Trade building bonuses; control section: ‘You keep those abilities even without control’; enemies do not gain them."},
    {"id":"Q27","answer":"Riverwalk is for the character and mechs: Rusviet can enter farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Nordic forests and mountains; Polania villages and mountains; Saxony forests and mountains. Nordic Swim is the starting special ability for workers alone: they may cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes. It does not help Nordic character/mechs.","support":"supported","evidence":"Faction/Riverwalk table; Nordic Swim: workers alone cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; does not help character/mechs."},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts are for characters and mechs, not workers.","support":"supported","evidence":"Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township descriptions both specify character/mech Move actions."},
    {"id":"Q29","answer":"Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or Saxony’s Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery may be used before combat by paying one power to reduce the opponent’s power by two, once per combat, not per unit.","support":"supported","evidence":"Saxony Underpass/Disarm and Nordic Seaworthy/Artillery ability descriptions."},
    {"id":"Q30","answer":"Two mechs and three workers allow three combat cards total with Rusviet People’s Army: one additional card total when at least one worker is present, on top of the two cards allowed for two participating mechs. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech must participate.","support":"supported","evidence":"People’s Army: one additional card total, still requiring character/mech; ‘Two mechs and three workers allow three cards’; workers alone never fight."},
    {"id":"Q31","answer":"With unlocked Wayfare, Crimea character/mechs may move from a territory or home base to its own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot enter an active opponent’s home base.","support":"supported","evidence":"Crimea Wayfare: destinations include own or any inactive faction home base; ‘not an active opponent’s base.’"},
    {"id":"Q32","answer":"Before combat, Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of the card’s value.","support":"supported","evidence":"Crimea Wayfare/Scout and Crimea starting special ability Coercion descriptions."},
    {"id":"Q33","answer":"Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and allows eligible units to retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but gives no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off; carried workers and resources cannot be left behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.","support":"supported","evidence":"Nordic Seaworthy and Polania Submerge descriptions; lake-carried pieces rule and explicit Polania retreat limitation."},
    {"id":"Q34","answer":"Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not protect against popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Camaraderie: ‘after you win combat as aggressor on your turn’; does not protect against loss for undefended workers."},
    {"id":"Q35","answer":"Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first option’s gain can pay the second option’s cost. The summary does not say Polania may choose more than two options or waive a cost.","support":"supported","evidence":"Polania Meander: ‘up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost.’"},
    {"id":"Q36","answer":"A character entering an encounter-token territory during Factory bottom Move stops and cannot move again that turn. Encounters are resolved after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; thus the encounter does not occur before all combats finish.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move encounter rule: character stops and cannot move again; resolve after whole Move action and all combats. Applies during Factory Move."},
    {"id":"Q37","answer":"Combat-card count is public but card contents are secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but a player need not reveal their total coin value. During combat, players may conceal whether they have committed cards until reveal.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup information disclosure paragraph: public combat-card count, secret contents/objectives, coin totals need not be revealed, combat commitment may be concealed."},
    {"id":"Q38","answer":"Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable in informal agreements; in tournament play even coin exchanges for deals or alliances are forbidden. Agreements are unenforceable. A payment cannot cancel combat once initiated by moving units onto opposing units: fight after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.","support":"supported","evidence":"Objectives and agreements: ‘unenforceable’; ‘Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable’; combat cannot be canceled once initiated; bribes may influence outcome."},
    {"id":"Q39","answer":"Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per controlled territory, $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. Popularity 7–12: $4 per star, $3 per territory, $2 per resource pair. Popularity 13–18: $5 per star, $4 per territory, $3 per resource pair. Controlled lakes count, home bases do not; a single leftover resource scores nothing because only complete pairs count.","support":"supported","evidence":"Final fortune table; controlled lakes count and home bases do not; ‘ignore an odd leftover token.’"},
    {"id":"Q40","answer":"For adjacency bonuses, count each qualifying feature only once across all your structures. Rivers do not break adjacency. Encounter locations count even after the encounter token has been removed. Tunnels are unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines; lakes are unique lakes. Payout for each bonus type (adjacent tunnels, lakes, or encounters): 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; 6 (or for lakes/encounters, 6–7) $9; zero features scores zero.","support":"supported","evidence":"Structure bonus table: unique features, Mines excluded, removed encounters count, rivers do not break adjacency; listed tiers/payouts."},
    {"id":"Q41","answer":"Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 $2; 2 $4; 3–4 $6. Structures in a row scores only your longest continuous straight line: 1 $2; 2 $4; 3 $6; 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras counts qualifying structures combined: 1 $2; 2 $4; 3 $6; 4 $9.","support":"supported","evidence":"Structure bonus table rows for structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras."},
    {"id":"Q42","answer":"Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: attacker loses popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, ‘even for workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.’"},
    {"id":"Q43","answer":"No. A placed star remains permanent if popularity later drops, but current popularity determines final scoring. The summary says each goal is awarded once and other players’ stars never block a goal; it does not state that two factions may both earn the same achievement.     {"id":"Q44","answer":"Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions.     {"id":"Q45","answer":"Rivers are borders between land hexes; lakes are entire territories adjoining the surrounding shores. Units normally cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Lake-capable character/mechs may move to/from lakes, but the summary does not specify from which particular surrounding land territories they may enter a lake; that detail is unsupported.","support":"partial","evidence":"Move: ‘Rivers are borders between land hexes; a lake is an entire territory adjoining the surrounding shores’; unlocked abilities give exceptions. Seaworthy/Submerge specify lake movement generally."},
    {"id":"Q46","answer":"No, the encounter card is not private: show it to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read its capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: ‘Show the encounter card to all players when drawn’, show artwork and read capitalized thematic text; no need to read every option."},
    {"id":"Q47","answer":"No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: ‘No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.’"},
    {"id":"Q48","answer":"The next player may begin while the current player completes a noninteractive bottom-action decision; players may overlap that decision with the next turn. Interactive bonuses and game-end priority must still be resolved in order.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: ‘Players may overlap a noninteractive bottom-action decision with the next turn, but resolve interactive bonuses and game-end priority in order.’"},
    {"id":"Q49","answer":"No. Each section’s top action and bottom action may each be taken at most once on that turn.     {"id":"Q50","answer":"You may choose the alternative Move benefit and gain $1 instead of moving units.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move OR coins: ‘Alternatively gain $1.’"},
    {"id":"Q51","answer":"No. The summary says workers never return to the Player Mat.     {"id":"Q52","answer":"Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: ‘You may attack with zero power/popularity.’"},
    {"id":"Q53","answer":"Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; you simply cannot earn further ordinary combat stars beyond that limit. Saxony has no usual limit within the six available stars.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: ‘You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit’; Saxony exception."},
    {"id":"Q54","answer":"For an ordinary faction, you normally choose one affordable option; the summary does not allow declining to choose an option after drawing. You cannot select an unaffordable coin or popularity option. You must pay the chosen option’s printed cost, but may take as little of its benefit as desired.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: ‘Normally choose one affordable option’; must pay printed cost; may take as little benefit as desired; unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected."},
    {"id":"Q55","answer":"No. Combatants choose their dials simultaneously and secretly, rather than in turn order. Dials and any played cards are revealed simultaneously.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat step 1: ‘Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose’; step 3: ‘Reveal simultaneously.’"},
    {"id":"Q56","answer":"Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: ‘Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.’"},
    {"id":"Q57","answer":"No. Star goals are placed as soon as achieved, and the sixth star immediately ends play. An objective is different: a completed objective may be held and revealed later, but only on your own turn and only while all its requirements are met at reveal.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars: ‘Place a star as soon as you achieve’; sixth star immediately ends play. Objectives: ‘You may wait’ to reveal a completed objective."},
    {"id":"Q58","answer":"Normally no. Units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; unlocked abilities provide exceptions. Unlocked abilities give exceptions below.’"},
    {"id":"Q59","answer":"No. The recruit is permanently placed on the Faction Mat one-time bonus space and cannot later move.","support":"supported","evidence":"Enlist: ‘put it permanently’ on a bonus; ‘It cannot later move.’"},
    {"id":"Q60","answer":"No. Only a character triggers an encounter. A mech or worker entering the territory does not resolve the encounter or remove its token.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: ‘Only a character triggers an encounter.’"},
    {"id":"Q61","answer":"A controlled Mill provides one additional Produce territory, beyond the up to two chosen controlled territories, and the Mill itself produces as one worker in addition to actual workers there. It can produce even when no actual worker is on its territory. If you do not control the Mill territory, it cannot produce.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce: controlled Mill ‘provides an additional bonus production territory and itself produces as one worker’; can work without actual worker; only while controlled."},
    {"id":"Q62","answer":"You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. If your last unit leaves and you have no structure, resources alone do not establish control; control requires a unit or qualifying structure presence.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control: ‘You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit.’"},
    {"id":"Q63","answer":"Build costs wood; Enlist costs food.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row resources: ‘Upgrade — oil; Deploy — metal; Build — wood; Enlist — food.’"}
  ]

    {"id":"Q01","answer":"Shuffle the Factory deck, randomly select players + 1 cards face-down onto the board, and return the rest to the box without looking.     {"id":"Q02","answer":"Character starts at home base; two workers start one per land-adjoined territory adjoining home; four mechs start over their Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures in matching boxes; four recruits in bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat. Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup steps 3–4 specify mat assignments and starting pieces."},
    {"id":"Q03","answer":"You must move the action token to a different section, but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section; otherwise sections cannot be repeated on consecutive turns.     {"id":"Q04","answer":"An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources.     {"id":"Q05","answer":"No. On a normal Move, up to two different units each move one adjacent territory; you cannot use both selections to move one unit twice.     {"id":"Q06","answer":"The Speed mech stops upon entering a territory occupied only by enemy workers, and cannot move again that turn.     {"id":"Q07","answer":"Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats.     {"id":"Q08","answer":"Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both deck and discards are empty draw none.     {"id":"Q10","answer":"Upgrade costs oil: move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box (not a solid-black-bordered red box), improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost.     {"id":"Q11","answer":"Build costs wood and places a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total per territory, including opponents'; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden.     {"id":"Q12","answer":"Take a recruit from any bottom-row section and permanently put it on any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards.     {"id":"Q13","answer":"Both combatants simultaneously and secretly set dial power from zero up to the smaller of seven and their current power, then may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech; Rusviet People's Army adds one card total if any workers are present.     {"id":"Q14","answer":"Winner controls territory/resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two, Saxony unrestricted within its six stars).     {"id":"Q19","answer":"If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star.     {"id":"Q01","answer":"Shuffle the Factory cards, randomly select players + 1 face-down onto the board, and return the rest to the box without looking.     {"id":"Q02","answer":"Place each character at its home base; place two workers on the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; place four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities; put six stars by the faction emblem; put six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with black squares; structures in their matching Player Mat boxes; recruits in the bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat ready for first placement.     {"id":"Q03","answer":"You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section; otherwise the section must differ from last turn.     {"id":"Q04","answer":"An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources.     {"id":"Q05","answer":"No. A normal Move can move up to two different units one adjacent territory each; the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice.     {"id":"Q06","answer":"A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero.     {"id":"Q07","answer":"After all units finish a Move action, resolve combats before the following bottom-row action. The attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: after all units finish a Move action, fights occur before any subsequent bottom action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order. Move rules restrict workers entering or leaving enemy character/mech-controlled territory alone."},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"Bolster costs $1 and gains either two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat draw deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both are empty draw none. Put traded resources on a controlled territory with at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bolster: pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card; empty deck reshuffle rule. Trade: pay $1, choose two resources or one popularity; resources placed on controlled territory containing a worker; cannot trade for resources if all workers at home."},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"Pay every exposed Produce cost in full, including power, popularity and/or coins, before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village after payment. You may decline some or all production, including new workers.     {"id":"Q10","answer":"Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; it moves a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered boxes cannot be upgraded). Costs vary with the mat and upgrades. Even after completing all such pieces, you may still pay for a bottom action to receive its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Upgrade and Deploy: pay exposed mat costs in oil/metal; stated effects and placement restrictions. Bottom-row actions: may still pay after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits."},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total can occupy a territory, including opponents' structures. The Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill gives its bonus production only while you control its territory; an enemy there can remove your control, so the Mill cannot produce then. A Mine is your personal tunnel for your unit movement even while an enemy occupies its territory. Opponents cannot use your buildings' abilities.","support":"supported","evidence":"Build: placement, one structure limit, no lakes/home bases, structures cannot be moved or destroyed. Mill only while controlled; Mine remains a personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled."},
    {"id":"Q12","answer":"Put the recruit token from any bottom-row section into any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat permanently, and immediately gain that chosen space's two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. When you, your immediate left, or immediate right neighbor takes the corresponding bottom action, resolve the active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor, stopping if a sixth star ends play. In a two-player game the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.","support":"supported","evidence":"Enlist and Ongoing recruits: permanent placement and one-time choices; circle uncovered determines ongoing bonus; active player then left then right; two-player opponent once."},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"Each combatant simultaneously and secretly chooses dial power from zero to the lesser of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including with zero dial power. If both sides have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first and defender second. Both deduct their selected dial power from their Power Track and discard played cards face-up; card values do not deduct track power.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 1–4: simultaneous secret dial selection, optional cards per character/mech, People's Army extra card, simultaneous reveal and tie rule, abilities order, and payment."},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"The winner controls the territory and its resources. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat (including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake); a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie's combat exception. A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat star places one, and with two places none; Saxony places a star after each victory while it has star tokens. You may keep fighting at the limit. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 5–6: control, retreat/resources, combat stars, popularity loss and losing-card reward."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; if contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token remains. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no additional normal action cost, and receive no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: only character triggers; after Move and all combats; token stays if contested entry lost; gains go to encounter territory; no normal action costs or mat bonuses."},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"Every player's character must choose one available Factory card on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory, after winning combat if necessary; this is not just the first player to visit. Each player gets one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. It acts as a fifth section with optional top then bottom, subject to the normal no-repeat rule except Rusviet. Similar Factory actions do not grant corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom Move action moves one unit up to two territories within that action, or up to three for a character/mech with Speed, subject to Mine access and normal stop restrictions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Factory: every character picks on first finish of Move there; one permanent card; fifth section; no mat/recruit/building bonuses; bottom Move distance and Speed."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"You may reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, and must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal; you may wait to reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the objective deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and can score both.","support":"supported","evidence":"Objectives and agreements: own turn timing, all requirements at reveal, both cards discarded to bottom, Saxony exception."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars normally), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars cannot be lost, and another player's star does not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play with no equalizing turns or further actions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars and immediate end lists every star goal, permanence, no blocking, and sixth-star ending."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"For a sixth star from a bottom-row action, first collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. Resolve recruit bonuses active player first, then left, then right, checking for a sixth star after each; if one ends the game, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars and immediate end: bottom action collection order, neighbor recruit sequence, and pending-battle movement rollback."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete resource pair. Five stars add $20. Four normal controlled territories plus the Factory count as seven, adding $21. Thirteen resources make six complete pairs, adding $12; total added to held coins is $53. Add the selected structure bonus from your structures even if enemies control their territories. Victory goes by total coins, then workers + mechs + structures, power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Final fortune: popularity 7–12 rates; Factory is three counts; complete pairs rounded down; structures qualify despite enemy control; listed tiebreakers."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"A home base is not a territory. Normally you cannot move back into any home base; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: home base is not a territory; entry exceptions and inactive expansion placeholders."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if necessary.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce terrain table; resources paragraph says workers are not resources and resource tokens have no supply limit."},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"Any unit can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources, including mid-movement; only mechs can carry your workers, and never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, so the added step can be before or after it. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: all units carry resources, mechs carry workers; Speed and tunnel jump step rules; stops override Speed."},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"Yes. Any unit may enter territory held only by an enemy structure and take control without combat. Printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move rules: entry into enemy-structure-only territory; all printed tunnels adjacent for any unit."},
    {"id":"Q25","answer":"You may not pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action. The token must move from the section used last turn, so after using Move you choose a different section.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: pay costs in full, never part; if unable to afford any action, move token to a different section and take neither."},
    {"id":"Q26","answer":"A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are future matching top-action bonuses from the uncovered structure benefits. You keep your structure abilities even without control of the territory, and enemy units do not gain them, so an enemy occupant does not take them away.","support":"supported","evidence":"Build structure effects; control rules say abilities remain without control except Mill production, and enemy units do not gain abilities."},
    {"id":"Q27","answer":"Riverwalk destinations for character/mechs are Rusviet: farms and villages; Crimea: farms and tundra; Nordic: forests and mountains; Polania: villages and mountains; Saxony: forests and mountains. These destinations apply to character/mechs. Nordic Swim lets workers cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not help Nordic character/mechs or mechs generally.","support":"supported","evidence":"Faction table identifies Riverwalk destinations; Nordic Swim description says workers alone, not lakes, and no help to character/mechs."},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.","support":"supported","evidence":"Unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township explicitly specify character/mech Move actions."},
    {"id":"Q29","answer":"Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine and makes the opponent lose two power on the track once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery is different: before combat you may pay one power to reduce the opponent's power by two, also once per combat, not per unit.","support":"supported","evidence":"Saxony Underpass/Disarm and Nordic Seaworthy/Artillery descriptions."},
    {"id":"Q30","answer":"Two mechs and three workers permit three combat cards total: the normal one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total from People's Army when at least one worker is present. Workers alone never fight; combat still requires a character or mech.","support":"supported","evidence":"Rusviet People's Army: two mechs and three workers allow three cards; combat rules require character/mech and workers alone never fight."},
    {"id":"Q31","answer":"Crimea Wayfare allows character/mechs to move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It does not allow entry to an active opponent home base.","support":"supported","evidence":"Crimea Wayfare description explicitly states destinations and excludes active opponent bases."},
    {"id":"Q32","answer":"Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of the card's value.","support":"supported","evidence":"Crimea Wayfare/Scout and Crimea starting Coercion descriptions."},
    {"id":"Q33","answer":"Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake; Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but Polania has no adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off, and a carrier cannot leave workers or resources behind on a lake. Both allow lake combat; neither permits building or deploying on lakes.","support":"supported","evidence":"Nordic Seaworthy and Polania Submerge descriptions; lake movement edge-case paragraph."},
    {"id":"Q34","answer":"Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not prevent popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Polania Camaraderie description states its combat condition and excludes loss for undefended workers."},
    {"id":"Q35","answer":"Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. Resolve each option in turn; the first gain may pay the second option's cost. The summary does not say Polania draws or uses two encounter cards; it specifies up to two options on one card.","support":"supported","evidence":"Meander: up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost."},
    {"id":"Q36","answer":"In a Factory bottom Move, a character entering an encounter-token territory stops and cannot continue moving that turn. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; the encounter does not happen before combats finish.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounter rules say character stops; after whole Move action and all combats; same rules apply during Factory Move."},
    {"id":"Q37","answer":"Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their exact total value when asked. Combat-card hand count is public, though during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal; card contents remain secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.","support":"supported","evidence":"Public and hidden information table."},
    {"id":"Q38","answer":"Informal agreements are unenforceable, and coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (with coin deal/alliances forbidden in tournament play). Negotiation cannot cancel combat once initiated by moving units onto opposing units; combat must be fought after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.","support":"supported","evidence":"Objectives and agreements section states exchange, enforceability and initiated combat rules."},
    {"id":"Q39","answer":"At popularity 0–6, score $3 per star, $2 per territory count, and $1 per complete resource pair; at 7–12, $4, $3, and $2; at 13–18, $5, $4, and $3. Controlled lakes count as territories; home bases do not. Only complete pairs score, so a single leftover resource scores nothing.","support":"supported","evidence":"Final fortune popularity table and territory/resource counting paragraphs."},
    {"id":"Q40","answer":"For adjacent-feature tiles, count unique printed tunnel territories (not Mines), unique lakes, or unique printed encounter locations (even when tokens have been removed); count each feature once across all structures. The summary does not specify a special exception for duplicate adjacency beyond uniqueness. Rivers do not break adjacency. For 1 feature pay $2; 2–3 pay $4; 4–5 pay $6; tunnels pay $9 at 6, while lakes and encounters pay $9 at 6–7. Zero scores $0.","support":"supported","evidence":"Structure bonus eligibility table gives qualifying unique features and payout bands; rivers do not break adjacency."},
    {"id":"Q41","answer":"Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pay $6. For structures in a row, count only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line; 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3 pays $6, 4 pays $9. For structures on farms/tundras, count combined qualifying structures; 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3 pays $6, 4 pays $9.","support":"supported","evidence":"Structure bonus table rows for structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras."},
    {"id":"Q42","answer":"Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat step 6 explicitly includes workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake."},
    {"id":"Q43","answer":"Placing a popularity star is permanent, but it does not protect current popularity or its final-scoring tier: current popularity at game end determines scoring.     {"id":"Q44","answer":"Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions.     {"id":"Q45","answer":"A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes.     {"id":"Q46","answer":"No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud.     {"id":"Q47","answer":"There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory."},
    {"id":"Q48","answer":"The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: next clockwise player may begin while current player decides which bottom-row item to gain after starting a noninteractive bottom-row action."},
    {"id":"Q49","answer":"No. The chosen top and bottom actions are each limited to once within a turn, including for Rusviet; Rusviet's repeat ability waives only the restriction on repeating a section used last turn.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure explicitly limits chosen top and bottom actions to once within the turn, including Rusviet."},
    {"id":"Q50","answer":"You may gain $1 instead of moving units with the normal, unupgraded Move top action.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1."},
    {"id":"Q51","answer":"No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; workers produced from a village come from the mat left to right. Move/combat: retreating workers go to their home base."},
    {"id":"Q52","answer":"Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat section: you may attack with zero power/popularity."},
    {"id":"Q53","answer":"Yes. You may still fight after reaching the two combat-star limit; a non-Saxony winner with two combat stars simply places no further combat star.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: non-Saxony winner with two combat stars places none; may still fight after limit."},
    {"id":"Q54","answer":"No. A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option and cannot decline to choose any option; unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected.     {"id":"Q55","answer":"No turn-order selection is specified: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose their dials, then reveal simultaneously after optional combat cards are selected.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 1–3: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose, then reveal simultaneously."},
    {"id":"Q56","answer":"Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses."},
    {"id":"Q57","answer":"No. A star is placed as soon as its goal is achieved; because the sixth star immediately ends play, you cannot delay or decline a star to avoid ending the game. Objectives: may wait to reveal, requirements must hold at reveal."},
    {"id":"Q58","answer":"Normally, no: units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide exceptions; Nordic Swim allows only workers to cross rivers to land terrain and not lakes.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move rules: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; faction/mech abilities are exceptions."},
    {"id":"Q59","answer":"No. Once placed on an open one-time recruit bonus on the Faction Mat, the recruit cannot later move.","support":"supported","evidence":"Enlist: recruit is put permanently on any open one-time bonus and cannot later move."},
    {"id":"Q60","answer":"No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not trigger or remove its token.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: only a character triggers an encounter."},
    {"id":"Q61","answer":"While controlled, a Mill adds one bonus production territory to the normal Produce allowance: two normal territories become up to three, or an upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four.     {"id":"Q62","answer":"You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; if your last unit leaves and you have no structure there, you no longer control it.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control definition: unit present, or your structure there with no enemy unit."},
    {"id":"Q63","answer":"Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: Upgrade—oil; Deploy—metal; Build—wood; Enlist—food."}
  ]

["Q29","Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: opponent loses two power on track, once per combat, not per unit. ["Q30","With at least one worker present, Rusviet People’s Army permits one additional combat card total; with two mechs and three workers, those two mechs can play three cards total. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech must participate.","supported","People’s Army; Combat."],

    {"id":"Q01","answer":"Shuffle and select players + 1 Factory cards face-down; return the rest without looking. Place one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup: Factory cards, structure bonus tile, 11 encounter tokens, lowest-numbered Player Mat starts."},
    {"id":"Q02","answer":"Place character at home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; four mechs over Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six technology cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objectives.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup, steps 3–4."},
    {"id":"Q03","answer":"You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither, either, or both actions. Rusviet may repeat its last section, but each top and bottom action remains limited to once that turn. Top-row gains may pay a bottom-row cost. If both actions are taken, top must precede bottom. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before choosing any amount of exposed green-box benefits; benefits may be declined. Costs and benefits are the exposed boxes on your mat, with bottom-row details varying by mat and upgrades.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: different section, optional actions, exposed red/green boxes."},
    {"id":"Q04","answer":"An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may spend resources from any territories you currently control, even to take an action elsewhere.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker control; structure abilities; spend from any controlled territories."},
    {"id":"Q05","answer":"No: a normal Move selects up to two different units and moves each one adjacent territory; one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker may subsequently move itself, or move onto a mech and be carried by its later move.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions—Move OR coins: two different units; carried worker may subsequently move."},
    {"id":"Q06","answer":"A Speed-enabled mech entering territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; the enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero. Your workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control the territory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions—Move: Enemy workers only; Speed stops for enemy units override Speed."},
    {"id":"Q07","answer":"After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs. Your character or mech may enter, but stops and cannot move again that turn.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions—Move: Enemy character/mechs; combat timing and attacker order."},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. If all workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions—Bolster and Trade."},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before producing. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Revealing new costs changes future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions—Produce, steps 1–3."},
    {"id":"Q10","answer":"Upgrade costs the oil shown in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the metal shown in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place a mech from your Faction Mat on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and all mechs, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy; completed bottom actions."},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"Build on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total per territory, including opponents' structures.     {"id":"Q12","answer":"Put the recruit permanently on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat and immediately take that space's bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. When you or an immediate left/right neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, resolve active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions—Enlist; Ongoing recruits."},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero to the lesser of seven and their current power, then may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (plus Rusviet's one additional card if workers are present). If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each pays the dial power selected from the Power Track; played cards are discarded face-up and their values do not cost track power.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules & Edge Cases—Combat, steps 1–4."},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"The winner controls the territory and resources. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; a winning defender loses none (Polania Camaraderie exception applies). A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat star places one; with two places none. Saxony places one after every victory while it has a star token. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules & Edge Cases—Combat, steps 5–6."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter only if the character remains on its token territory. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay no normal action cost and gain no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules & Edge Cases—Encounters."},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after any combat), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one and returns the rest. Factory actions do not grant corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories in that Move action, or three for a Speed character/mech; Mine access and normal movement/stops still apply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules & Edge Cases—Factory."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"Only on your own turn, before or after a top or bottom action, reveal a completed objective; you must meet all its requirements at the moment of reveal, though you may wait. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the deck. Normally only one objective star. Saxony keeps the second card after the first and may score both.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules & Edge Cases—Objectives and agreements."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"Stars are awarded for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent, and another player's star does not block the goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scoring / Victory Conditions—Stars and immediate end."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"For a bottom-row action that earns the sixth star, first collect the primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. For a neighbor recruit star, finish the active action, then check active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for game end at each step. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement and return initiating units to their prior territories; do not resolve another combat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scoring—The sixth star immediately ends play; neighbor sequence and unresolved battle."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"At 10 popularity the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus the Factory are 7 territory counts and add $21; 13 resources make six pairs and add $12. Together these categories add $53 to held coins, before the selected structure bonus. Structures earn that bonus even if enemies control their territories. Ties break by workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Final fortune table; structure bonus eligibility; victory tie breaks."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"A home base is not a territory. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there or deploy there; setup, forced retreats and Crimea's unlocked Wayfare are exceptions. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources.     {"id":"Q23","answer":"All units can pick up, carry and drop any number of resources during movement; only mechs can also carry your workers, never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, with the extra step before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions—Move OR coins: carrying; Speed."},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"Yes. Any unit may enter a territory occupied only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat.     {"id":"Q25","answer":"You cannot pay only part of a cost. Nordic/Saxony cross rivers onto forests and mountains; Rusviet onto farms and villages; Crimea onto farms and tundra; Polania onto villages and mountains. Nordic Swim is a starting ability for workers alone to cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; it does not grant this ability to Nordic mechs.","support":"supported","evidence":"Faction and unlocked mech abilities: Riverwalk table; Nordic Swim."},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move.     {"id":"Q29","answer":"Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or its Mine, reducing the opponent's Power Track by two; once per combat, not per unit.     {"id":"Q30","answer":"Two mechs and three workers allow three combat cards total with Rusviet People's Army: the normal one per participating character/mech plus one extra card total if at least one worker is present.     {"id":"Q31","answer":"Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to Crimea's own or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases.     {"id":"Q32","answer":"Crimea Scout, before combat, steals one random combat card from the opponent into Crimea's hand, once per combat, not per unit.     {"id":"Q33","answer":"Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes, and permits retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them.     {"id":"Q34","answer":"Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn.     {"id":"Q35","answer":"Polania Meander allows up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; the first gain can pay the second option's cost.     {"id":"Q36","answer":"No. A character entering an encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move.     {"id":"Q37","answer":"Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their total value when asked.     {"id":"Q38","answer":"Players may make informal, unenforceable agreements; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances).     {"id":"Q40","answer":"Each qualifying adjacent feature counts once across all structures. Rivers do not break adjacency. Adjacent encounter locations count even after their token is removed.     {"id":"Q41","answer":"Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pay $6.     {"id":"Q42","answer":"Yes.     {"id":"Q43","answer":"No. A popularity star stays placed if popularity later drops, but current popularity determines final scoring.     {"id":"Q45","answer":"A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline.     {"id":"Q50","answer":"You may gain $1 instead of moving units with the normal unupgraded Move action.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions—Move OR coins."},
    {"id":"Q51","answer":"No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; a worker forced to retreat goes to its home base.     {"id":"Q52","answer":"Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: You may attack with zero power/popularity."},
    {"id":"Q53","answer":"Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; a non-Saxony winner with two combat stars places no further combat star.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat-star award: may still fight after reaching combat-star limit."},
    {"id":"Q54","answer":"No to declining all options and no to unaffordable options: a faction without Meander must choose one affordable option.     {"id":"Q55","answer":"No turn order selection: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose their dials and optionally cards. Reveal simultaneously after both have chosen.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 1–3: simultaneously and secretly choose; reveal simultaneously."},
    {"id":"Q56","answer":"Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses."},
    {"id":"Q57","answer":"No. Place a star as soon as its goal is achieved; a sixth star immediately ends play.     {"id":"Q58","answer":"By default, units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions—Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes."},
    {"id":"Q59","answer":"No. The recruit is placed permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat and cannot later move.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions—Enlist: permanently; it cannot later move."},
    {"id":"Q60","answer":"No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering does not trigger or remove the token.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: Only a character triggers an encounter."},
    {"id":"Q61","answer":"While controlled, the Mill adds one bonus production territory to your normal allowance: two becomes up to three, or an upgraded three becomes up to four.
